insider_note: One of the most repeated VSAQs in the paper — six printed appearances. Two words carry it: separation and purification.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Downstream processing defined
steps.margin_note: Definition with both operations named. Five lines.
lines: DOWNSTREAM PROCESSING is everything done to
a biotechnology product AFTER the biosynthetic
stage, before it is ready for marketing.
Its two main operations are SEPARATION and
steps.why: A product made inside a tank of cells is mixed with everything else in the tank, so it has to be separated out before it is of any use.
common_mistakes: Saying downstream processing is part of making the product. It comes AFTER.
Naming one operation. Separation AND purification are both needed.
steps.memory_tip: Everything after the making, before the selling.

steps.label: What it includes
steps.margin_note: The additional stages listed. Six lines.
lines: Only then is the product released for sale.
steps.why: A biological product has to be proved both pure and safe, which is why testing is part of the process rather than an afterthought.
common_mistakes: Stopping at purification. Preservatives, trials and quality control are all part of it.
Saying it applies only to medicines. Every biotechnology product goes through it.
steps.memory_tip: Nothing is released until it has been tested.
